paper_metadata.title: A Field Programmable Analog Array for CMOS Continuous-Time OTA-C Filter Applications
paper_metadata.abstract: A programmable high-frequency operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) is proposed and analyzed. A possibility to build filters of frequencies from several kilohertz general configurable analog block (CAB) is presented, which up to several megahertz. The structure of the FPAA is composed consists of the proposed programmable OTA, programmable of universal configurable analog blocks (CABs). The proposed capacitor and MOSFET switches. Using the CABs, the universal FPAA consists of 40 CABs. A tuning circuit compensating for tunable and field programmable analog array (FPAA) can be process variations, temperature, power supply, bias change, constructed, which can realize many signal-processing functions, including filters. A tuning circuit is also discussed. The proposed etc., is also considered. As examples, implementations of an OTA has been simulated and fabricated in CMOS technology. RLC ladder-based sixth-order bandpass filter and a fourth-order The results show that the OTA has the transconductance tuncascaded biquad filter are presented. able/programmable in a wide range of 700 times and the 3-dB bandwidth larger than 20 MHz.
